fact_check.claim: 2026-27 minimum for TA/GA/RA/GRA: $48,912 12-month ($36,684 nine-month + $12,228 summer), effective August 21, 2026
fact_check.note: Page lists exactly these figures and the August 21, 2026 effective date.

fact_check.claim: About $4,076 a month before taxes; 12-month stipend about $3,250 under $52,166 living-wage line
fact_check.note: 48,912/12 = 4,076; 25.08 x 2,080 = 52,166; gap 3,254. Arithmetic is correct and labeled as ours.

fact_check.claim: Tompkins County living wage for a single adult 2026 is $25.08/hour
fact_check.note: Page gives $25.08 for a single adult without children on a 2,080-hour year. It has no food, phone or transport breakdown, and the article does not claim one.

fact_check.claim: 2025-26 12-month stipend $47,548; 2026-27 is $1,364 higher, about 2.9 percent
fact_check.note: Page gives $47,548. Difference and percentage are correct.

fact_check.claim: University Fellowship summer $7,779, 12-month $44,463; Cornell Tech $60,719
fact_check.note: Matches the page.

fact_check.claim: Cap of $55,025 academic year and $18,341 summer if any part comes from Cornell-held funds
fact_check.note: Matches the page.

fact_check.claim: Assistantships average 15 hours a week, up to 5 more permitted
fact_check.note: Matches the page.

fact_check.claim: Doctoral funding includes tuition, fees, SHP and stipend; summer stipends are offered by some programs in addition
fact_check.note: Page says this.

fact_check.claim: Assistantship pay has taxes withheld; fellowship stipends are refunds to the student account with no taxes withheld and typically taxable
fact_check.note: Page says assistantship taxes are withheld and fellowship taxes are not withheld, so students plan for them at filing. 'Typically taxable' is a mild paraphrase.

fact_check.claim: Students on assistantships and fellowships are enrolled in the SHP at no cost
fact_check.note: Page confirms.

fact_check.claim: SHP 2026-27 is $4,092 for fully funded graduate students; spouse/partner or one child $4,092, two or more children $8,184
fact_check.note: Matches the July-start (12-month) column. The August-start (11-month) amounts differ ($3,751 and $7,502); the article does not mention that.

fact_check.claim: Hasbrouck 2026-27 monthly: regular single in 2-bedroom townhouse $620 (furnished), studio $1,355, 1-bedroom unfurnished $1,415; 12-month contract
fact_check.note: Rates match; the townhouse is listed only as furnished, as the table says.

fact_check.claim: Housing rates include gas, electricity, garbage pickup and internet up to 200 GB a month
fact_check.note: Matches the page.

fact_check.claim: Zumper Oct. 2026: one-bedroom averages $1,695, studio $1,725 (market rent near Cornell)
fact_check.note: The figures are right, but the fetched page says its averages are for Trumansburg, a village about 20 miles from campus, not Ithaca or Cornell. The article says only that the page 'also mentions Trumansburg'. The meta description, the table row, the 42 percent figure and the 'single and want your own place' advice all rest on this number as an Ithaca market one-bedroom. The studio above the one-bedroom is flagged as a thin sample, which the article does say.

fact_check.claim: RentCafe Collegetown, as of October 30, 2026: studio $2,006, 1-bedroom $2,342, 2-bedroom $3,414
fact_check.note: Matches the page and date. The page also lists sizes (148 sq ft studio), which suggest a thin sample; the article does not mention this.
Recomputed: all correct to rounding and labeled as our arithmetic.

fact_check.claim: CRS May 2026 report defines cost-burdened as spending more than 30 percent of income on housing; the benchmark HUD uses; 30% of $48,912 is about $1,223 a month
fact_check.note: Report R48945 is dated May 13, 2026, defines cost burden at over 30%, and cites HUD (footnote to HUD's Worst Case Housing Needs report). The article uses the CRS report rather than a hud.gov link, which is an acceptable official source. 48,912 x 0.30 / 12 = 1,223.

fact_check.claim: Nine-month-only: $36,684 is about $3,057 a month over the year; $1,355 studio is 44 percent, $1,695 one-bedroom 55 percent
fact_check.note: Arithmetic correct (the 55 percent uses the Trumansburg-based Zumper rent; see the Zumper mismatch).

fact_check.claim: Johnson MBA fall/spring budget: meals $5,768, transportation $3,754, miscellaneous $4,196; months not stated
fact_check.note: Figures are on the page for the Fall/Spring term 2026-27; the page does not state months, as the article says. Using an MBA budget as a proxy for a PhD student is flagged as an estimate.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Global Learning living-expense estimate $37,418 for 2026-27, $3,118 a month (international graduate students)
fact_check.note: Page gives $37,418 over 12 months and $3,118 a month.

fact_check.claim: Non-rent estimate $830 to $1,110 a month and the resulting leftover ranges ($1,600-$1,900 studio; $1,270-$1,550 market one-bedroom)
fact_check.note: Arithmetic correct and labeled as our estimate. The market one-bedroom leftover depends on the Zumper figure.

fact_check.claim: Union fee is 1.44 percent of stipend, about $704 a year or $59 a month; payroll deduction only after signing an authorization; otherwise pay the union directly
fact_check.note: Official Graduate School page cites the union website for 1.44% and confirms the authorization-form and direct-payment points. 48,912 x 1.44% = 704.

fact_check.claim: Charity option: sincerely held religious, moral or ethical objection; monthly donation equal to dues; American Heart Association, American Cancer Society, United Way
fact_check.note: Matches the page.

fact_check.claim: NLRB challenge to the union is pending, reported by the Sun in March 2026, no ruling reported
fact_check.note: Article dated March 4, 2026 describes a pending appeal filed Feb. 10, 2026 and reports no ruling.

fact_check.claim: Graduate student workers in Ithaca get free TCAT passes; September 2025 notice says doctoral students are eligible for an OmniRide pass for all years of study; request by emailing transportation@cornell.edu
fact_check.note: Official page says both. It words eligibility differently in the two places, and the article tells readers to confirm with Transportation Services.

fact_check.claim: $544 benefits adjustment in the Ithaca minimum stipend for fall 2025 and fall 2026, covering dental, vision and fitness center access; for graduate student workers, not fellows
fact_check.note: Page describes the adjustment as included in the Ithaca minimum for both falls and as applying to bargaining-unit workers. (The page quotes $48,911 for fall 2026 against the stipend page's $48,912, a one-dollar difference between Cornell pages that the article does not rely on.)

fact_check.claim: Base stipend rates are the same for fellowships and assistantships and do not vary by discipline
fact_check.note: Page says rates are consistent across graduate fields.

fact_check.claim: Ewa Nizalowska, a Ph.D. student in Government, argued in a March 2023 Sun guest column that the 8 percent raise did not keep up with Ithaca costs; she cited a study showing Tompkins County rents rose 12.3 percent
fact_check.note: The argument and the 12.3% rent figure are in the column with no time period, and the article now words it correctly. The fetch confirmed that the author is a Ph.D. student but did not return her field, so 'in Government' could not be checked.

fact_check.claim: Cornell's 8 percent raise was the largest jump in stipends since 2006; 1.4 percent of graduating doctoral students in 2022 had borrowed, against a 38.5 percent national average for doctoral research graduates
fact_check.note: Matches the Chronicle announcement.

beats_top.query: cornell grad student stipend cost of living Ithaca enough
beats_top.why: The first search result was a 2016 Sun article, and the strongest official result is the Graduate School rates page. Both give only rates or opinion and no rent-versus-stipend budget. Our page answers in the first paragraph and works through rent, the summer gap, fees and dependents.
changes: Replace the Zumper figure with an Ithaca-specific market rent, or drop the market one-bedroom row and rewrite the meta description and the 'single and want your own place' advice.
Keep the RentCafe Collegetown figures, noting that they come from a small sample of small units.
